a18.speaker: Edgar Chibaka, UK-MCC Chairperson & Co-founder
a18.speech: Described the launch as a "defining moment for Malawi–Scotland relations." "This is about building a new era of economic collaboration through diaspora-led initiatives," ; "We're honoured to welcome Hon. Mumba and other distinguished guests to Edinburgh to celebrate this shared vision."

a18.speaker: Dr. Thomas Bisika, Malawi High Commissioner to the UK and Patron of UK-MCC
a18.speech: "Malawi is open for business," ; "As we work toward becoming a self-reliant, upper middle-income country, trade and investment will be central to that journey."

a18.speaker: Stuart Brown, CEO of the Scotland Malawi Partnership
a18.speech: Hailed the launch as a natural extension of the longstanding people-to-people ties between the two nations. "This initiative brings economic opportunity into the heart of our historic partnership," ; "It's about ethical, inclusive trade that benefits both Malawi and Scotland for generations to come."

a49.speaker: FBC Securities (financial analysts)
a49.speech: Warned that local capital markets — the Zimbabwe Stock Exchange (ZSE) and Victoria Falls Stock Exchange (VFEX) — could eventually be affected by the United States' foreign aid freeze, imposed via an Executive Order on Reevaluating and Realigning United States Foreign Aid that suspended all foreign assistance for 90 days.

a50.speaker: Eliud Kireger, Director-General of the Kenya Agricultural and Livestock Research Institute (Kalro)
a50.speech: Says aflatoxin is rampant in the lower eastern region and parts of Tana River County because of high humidity. Says aflatoxin is not just a risk to the health of Kenyans but also a threat to their economic wellbeing. "The adoption of this bio-control technology with other management practices by farmers will reduce aflatoxin contamination by over 70 per cent in maize and groundnut and increase crop value by at least five per cent." Said they had planned to supply Aflasafe alongside other farm inputs this year in a countrywide rollout plan.

a50.speaker: Charity Mutegi (Dr. Mutegi), East Africa Aflasafe Coordinator
a50.speech: Says adoption of this bio-control tool will go a long way in curbing this menace. "If applied properly and combined with good agricultural practices, Aflasafe effectively controls aflatoxin during crop development and post-harvesting."

a50.speaker: Kenya Agricultural and Livestock Research Institute (Kalro) (cited data)
a50.speech: About 150 people from lower Eastern Kenya who consumed highly contaminated maize during the 2004 and 2005 cropping seasons died from the effects of aflatoxin.

a56.speaker: Richard M. Mills, US Ambassador to Nigeria
a56.speech: Writes that for two decades the United States has stood with Nigeria in the fight against HIV/AIDS under PEPFAR, investing more than $8.3 billion in Nigeria's health sector and providing life-saving anti-retroviral treatment to more than 1.5 million people. Argues that positive health outcomes depend on good governance, and that the US supports initiatives to enhance transparency, accountability, and human rights in Nigeria. States that U.S.-supported initiatives have helped strengthen pharmaceutical supply chains and empowered civil society organizations to advocate for marginalized communities, and reaffirms that the United States continues to stand with the Nigerian people and their government.

a56.speaker: United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime (cited survey)
a56.speech: According to a recent survey, Nigerians are both more frequently refusing to pay bribes and reporting bribe seekers to investigative journalists and rule of law authorities.

a207.speaker: United Nations
a207.speech: Said it is forced to close all the bakeries in Gaza, because of the flour shortage resulting from Israel's blockade of the territory. These bakeries were essential for feeding thousands of Gazans.

a207.speaker: Spokesperson for the UN World Food Programme
a207.speech: Said this closure will affect hundreds of thousands of Palestinians who depend on baked bread.

a207.speaker: Humanitarian agencies
a207.speech: Are now warning that the halt of aid could cause a major catastrophe.

a207.speaker: Israeli government / Israeli forces
a207.speech: Are attempting to defend the killing of health workers who were killed inside an emergency response vehicle, and have tried to defend the action they carried out in Gaza a week earlier when their forces opened fire on a vehicle convoy, killing fifteen health workers, civil defence workers and a United Nations staff member.

a486.speaker: Ruqia Balkhi, 55-year-old Afghan engineer resettled in the US
a486.speech: "It was completely opposite for my husband," she said of the circumstances he faced; explained that her husband was luckier than most, given that he had a family already established in the US, but expressed anguish for those entering the country without the same support system she received ; "Without help from the resettlement agency, I don't think we would have been able to survive" ; "My request from the new government is that they not forget their commitments to Afghan allies and Afghan immigrants."

a486.speaker: Advocates (unnamed)
a486.speech: Say her family's story illustrates how Trump's broad executive orders might have repercussions even for areas of bipartisan support.

a486.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a486.speech: Campaign promises made no secret of his desire to overhaul the US immigration system, to fend off what he decried as a migrant "invasion"; repeatedly expressed sympathy for those caught up in the August 2021 troop withdrawal; blasted former US President Joe Biden for overseeing the incident, which he called the "Afghanistan calamity."

a486.speaker: Shawn VanDiver, founder of #AfghanEvac
a486.speech: "President Trump campaigned on a bunch of stuff related to Afghanistan, particularly how bad the withdrawal was. So I just don't believe that he would do that and then not try to help our allies. I'm just hoping this is a mistake" ; said Trump's actions from here forward will be critical: "But if they don't change anything, well, then you can be left to conclude that maybe they did mean to do it."

a486.speaker: Shawn VanDiver, founder of #AfghanEvac
a486.speech: Explained that the State Department's freeze on foreign aid has gutted services for those waiting abroad in places like Qatar and Albania, including medical care, food and legal support ; "The shutdown of these services isn't just an inconvenience. It could be a death sentence for some of the most vulnerable evacuees."

a486.speaker: US administration stop-work order to resettlement organisations
a486.speech: Earlier this month, 10 national organisations that rely on federal support to provide "reception and placement services" received an order to stop work immediately - and incur no further costs.

a486.speaker: Kim Staffieri, executive director of the Association of Wartime Allies
a486.speech: Said individuals seeking refuge through the refugee programmes should receive the same urgent attention as SIV recipients: "There are a lot of people that helped us, who worked for the same goals over there that are very much in danger, but they just don't qualify for the SIV because it's got such tight requirements on" ; said she expected Trump's administration to have given more consideration to Afghan refugees, given the bipartisan support for them: "We expected some challenges. What we didn't expect were these broad, sweeping strokes of pausing and suspending necessary programmes" ; "It feels like either they didn't have knowledge or they didn't take time to really think what the downstream effects would be in their entirety."

a486.speaker: NPR and Ipsos poll, September 2021
a486.speech: Suggested that two-thirds of US respondents backed the relocations of Afghans, far outpacing support for other groups seeking refuge.

a486.speaker: With Honor advocacy group poll, October 2023
a486.speech: Found that 80 percent of respondents signalled continuing support for Afghan resettlement.

a486.speaker: Pew Research Center
a486.speech: About 61 percent of veterans supported Trump in the 2024 election, according to the Pew Research Center.

a486.speaker: Andrew Sullivan, chief of advocacy and government affairs of No One Left Behind
a486.speech: Described the support for Afghan resettlement as "a matter of national honour and of national security" ; "It is certainly a veterans issue. And so it's been a bipartisan issue" ; said he was optimistic Trump would eventually create "carve-outs" for Afghans, pointing to the large number of veterans from the Afghanistan conflict in the Republican's administration; explained he has repeatedly engaged with Waltz on the issue and left feeling hopeful: "He understands on that personal, visceral level, how much these folks mean to [veterans]. So I know he gets it."

a486.speaker: Mike Waltz, former Congressman and Trump's White House national security adviser
a486.speech: Previously put pressure on former President Biden to "bring home our Afghan allies."

a486.speaker: James Powers, grassroots organiser from Ohio focused on veterans issues
a486.speech: Pointed to immigration hardliner Stephen Miller's role in the new administration: "It only makes sense that [the programme] would come to a screeching halt as soon as he got back into power to influence the current president" ; "They've got to do a better job. There are fair experts on both sides of the aisle, on all ideological spectrums, that will tell them there are better ways."

a682.speaker: Dr. Kalumbi Shangula, Minister of Health and Social Services of Namibia
a682.speech: Highlighted that Namibia has been battling the HIV and AIDS epidemic for about 37 years now, since the first case of HIV was detected in 1986: "Based on the latest spectrum estimates, Namibia has achieved 92%-99%-94% of the UNAIDS 95-95-95 target... Among the estimated PLHIV, 92% are aware of their HIV status. Among PLHIV who are aware of their HIV status, 99% are on ART. Among PLHIV on ART, 94% are virally suppressed. In summary, Namibia has surpassed the second 95% target and is close to achieving the first and third 95% targets. Congratulations, Namibia!"

a682.speaker: Dr. Kalumbi Shangula, Minister of Health and Social Services of Namibia
a682.speech: Stressed that the fight is not yet over and that the aim is to end AIDS as a Public Health Threat by 2030: "The Ministry has recently completed the review of the National Strategic Framework (NSF) for HIV/AIDS, interrogated data, and had conversations with all stakeholders up to the community level to understand how far we have gone in the response and also to get a better understanding of who is left behind in this response. As a result, a new National Strategic Framework for 2023-2024 to 2027-2028 is finalized and will be launched soon."

a734.speaker: Office of the President of South Sudan
a734.speech: Said President Salva Kiir Mayardit has sworn in new officials, including Dr. Riek Gai Kok as the new Governor of Jonglei State, Nyuol Justin Yaac as Chairperson of the Human Rights Commission, and Ezekia Alfandi Gibson as his deputy, in a ceremony at the Presidential Palace on Monday.

a734.speaker: Salva Kiir Mayardit, President of South Sudan
a734.speech: In his remarks, reportedly urged Governor Riek Gai to address the pressing issues in Jonglei State and pledged full support from his administration to tackle the ongoing instability in the region.

a734.speaker: Officials (unnamed, at the swearing-in ceremony)
a734.speech: Are reported to have encouraged Governor Gai to intensify efforts to ensure peace, stability, and unity in this volatile area.

a734.speaker: Riek Gai Kok, Governor of Jonglei State, South Sudan
a734.speech: Emphasised his commitment to collaborating with all segments of society in Jonglei to confront the numerous challenges facing the state.

a1089.speaker: International Organization for Migration (IOM)
a1089.speech: Launched an appeal for USD 77.6 million to provide humanitarian assistance to more than 1.2 million internally displaced persons (IDPs), returnees, host community members and migrants in Ethiopia.

a1089.speaker: Ester Ruiz de Azua, IOM Ethiopia's Emergency and Post-Crisis Programme Coordinator
a1089.speech: "IOM Ethiopia plans to provide support following two principal objectives: saving lives while responding to the humanitarian crisis and supporting the transition and recovery of crisis-affected communities."

a1312.speaker: International Monetary Fund (IMF) (communiqué published 9 November 2024)
a1312.speech: Reported that in Niger the economic outlook is favourable in the short term, with growth projected at 8.8% for 2024, growth that will be “supported by oil exports, the lifting of sanctions and a good agricultural season”; the document added that “the authorities' continued efforts to simplify the tax system and adopt a strategy for managing oil revenues are essential reforms to create fiscal space to meet development spending needs.” ; However, the IMF warned, “this positive outlook is subject to downside risks.”

a1312.speaker: International Monetary Fund (IMF) (communiqué published 9 November 2024)
a1312.speech: “Growth is projected at 8.8% in 2024, driven mainly by oil exports, a favourable agricultural season and the lifting of sanctions. Economic activity should remain dynamic next year, with growth reaching 7.9%, while inflation should fall back to 3.7%.” ; Cautioned: “Nevertheless, the risks surrounding this outlook are tilted to the downside. A deterioration in security conditions could further weigh on economic activity, while fiscal space could shrink if regional financing conditions continue to tighten.” ; “Other external risks include the volatility of commodity prices and the economic fallout of an escalation of regional conflicts (such as tensions in the Middle East).”

a1312.speaker: Antonio David, head of the IMF delegation/mission to Niger
a1312.speech: At the end of the mission, stated that “the Nigerien authorities and the IMF team have reached a staff-level agreement on the sixth review of the economic programme supported by the Extended Credit Facility, on the second review of the arrangement under the Resilience and Sustainability Facility, and have conducted the 2024 Article IV consultations.” ; “The staff-level agreement will be submitted for the approval of IMF Management and the Executive Board. The Board meeting on the RSF under Article IV is scheduled for December 2024. Completion of the ECF review would allow a disbursement of SDR 13.16 million (about $17.4 million, or 10% of Niger's quota) to cover the country's external financing needs.” ; “In addition, completion of the second review of the arrangement under the RSF would allow an additional disbursement of SDR 25.66 million (about $34 million, or 19.5% of Niger's quota).” ; “Despite a difficult context owing to factors such as the human and material consequences of the recent floods, liquidity pressures in the banking sector and tight financing conditions, a strong recovery in economic activity is expected this year.”

a1343.speaker: Olavo Correia, Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Finance and Business Development and Minister of the Digital Economy of Cabo Verde
a1343.speech: Explained that the fund is to be created through the debt that Cabo Verde owes to Portugal, amounting to 12 million contos, which will now be invested in this new instrument; asserted that for now it is a financial operation that is "innovative, but at the same time simple", highlighting the recognition the instrument is receiving from the World Bank and the International Monetary Fund (IMF). "That is, we will be able to invest in climate and the environment without increasing public debt, by way of this swap of debt for investment in climate," explained Olavo Correia.

a1343.speaker: Antonio Monteiro, deputy of the Cape Verdean Independent and Democratic Union (UCID, opposition)
a1343.speech: Somewhat sceptical, questioned the impact the fund could have given Cabo Verde's weight relative to the world; based on the figures presented by the deputy prime minister, he recalled that the country will need approximately 340 million contos by 2050, which in annual terms means spending of around 13.5 million contos. "Now, that is a lot of money for us to be able to decarbonise our country," he stressed, arguing that parallel work should be done with the most polluting countries. "If the world as a whole and, above all, the most developed [countries], do nothing, no matter how much we run, no matter how much work we do, we will be severely battered, both by the rise in sea levels and by all the environmental impacts arising from it," he said. According to him, Cabo Verde must be able to "pressure" the other countries to follow the same example, at the risk of the investment in the fund being made "with a greater burden in terms of State spending" while it "will not save the archipelago".

a1343.speaker: Juliao Varela, deputy of the African Party for the Independence of Cape Verde (PAICV, opposition)
a1343.speech: Considered that this instrument is "one more vehicle for increasing public debt". "It was said here that the fund may resort to external financing to leverage and make investments, and this has to be recorded somewhere as public debt, because it is a public fund," he stressed. He charged that the Government's idea is to "hide the public debt in the fund, as was already done with the INPS [National Social Security Institute]", because, he insisted, "there are many State debts that are currently on the balance sheet of the INPS, which was forced to buy State bonds".

a1343.speaker: Colmeia Association (petition)
a1343.speech: Petitioned the National Assembly requesting the adoption of legislative measures to improve the living conditions of people with disabilities.

a1411.speaker: World Bank
a1411.speech: Deems public debt of about 82 percent of GDP a level that is "in distress".

a1411.speaker: One development expert (anonymous)
a1411.speech: As one development expert lamented, Malawi's situation has worsened partly due to "too much aid, misinterpreted as development," which has "discouraged local agency at all levels".

a1411.speaker: Researchers
a1411.speech: Researchers have found that in highly aid-dependent countries, aid disbursements often coincide with sharp increases in deposits to offshore bank accounts, a sign that some of the funds are siphoned off by elites.

a1411.speaker: World Bank's latest Malawi Economic Monitor (report, 'The rising cost of inaction')
a1411.speech: Warns that the recovery remains "fragile due to lagging implementation of macroeconomic reforms" ; notes that without proactive measures, Malawi's debt and instability will only mount.

a1549.speaker: Isaac Stephens, Liberia Revenue Authority (LRA) Assistant Commissioner for Taxpayer Services
a1549.speech: Said this year's ceremony is being held under the theme "Moving to Billions", a target goal of the LRA this year. He made the disclosure on Wednesday, November 13, 2024, in an interview on the Super Morning Show.

a2155.speaker: Ambassador Lim, Korean Ambassador to Ethiopia
a2155.speech: "to beat COVID-19 and to recover from the devastation it has wrought, an unprecedented level of global solidarity and coordinated action is needed. The Korean government is prepared to fully share all information and insight garnered in our ongoing fight against COVID-19 with the partners in the international community. In particular, it will strengthen cooperation with Ethiopia, the only country in Africa that had dispatched a ground troop during the Korean War." ; He added that Korea will not forget the partnership which Ethiopia showed to protect peace and freedom, and both countries have currently been working towards a joint effort to fight the new enemy, COVID-19, to emerge victorious.

a2155.speaker: Lia Tadesse, Ethiopian Minister of Health
a2155.speech: Expressed her gratitude for the continuous support and solidarity by the Korean government and the Korean community in Ethiopia. The Minister added that "Ethiopia is proud of Korea, a close partner, that it has successfully overcome the COVID-19 crisis," and that "we hope Korea to play a crucial role in response to the COVID-19 in Africa, and especially in Ethiopia."

a2309.speaker: Scott Perry, US Congressman
a2309.speech: stated that the United States Agency for International Development (USAID) funded terrorist organisations, including Boko Haram.

a2309.speaker: Professors Kyari Mohammed, Jibrin Ibrahim, Usman Tar and Chris Kwaja, Dr. Atta Barkindo, Abdulbasit Kassim and other scholars
a2309.speech: have extensively researched and reported the origins and evolution of Boko Haram.

a2372.speaker: Hakainde Hichilema, President of Zambia
a2372.speech: Urged African nations to accelerate the development of regional power interconnectors, stressing that improved energy cooperation is critical to driving food security through irrigation and powering industrial growth ; said Africa must dismantle "artificial boundaries" in the power sector by investing in cross-border infrastructure that will enable electricity sharing across regions.

a2372.speaker: Elvis Nkandu, acting Energy Minister of Zambia
a2372.speech: Hailed the pact as a milestone in regional collaboration, noting that it covers not only electricity but also petroleum products. "We need to ensure we have the infrastructure to transmit energy both ways, while also expanding cooperation in downstream petroleum supplies," he said.

a2372.speaker: Bogolo Joy Kenewendo, Botswana's Minister of Electricity and Energy
a2372.speech: Described the deal as critical to strengthening the Southern African Power Pool. "When our infrastructure is weak, the entire region is compromised. This MoU marks a shift in how we cooperate and develop together," she said, urging partners to support feasibility studies, power plant construction, and distribution networks.

a2499.speaker: Gomezgani Zakazaka, Football Association of Malawi (FAM) competitions and communications director
a2499.speech: Said there will be no window for the Scorchers' international friendly matches up to the day of the Angola tie.

a2499.speaker: Lovemore Fazili, Scorchers coach
a2499.speech: Said they are not worried because the eight international friendly matches they had this year against Zambia, South Africa, Morocco, Ghana and Lesotho helped them to identify all areas that need improvement: "Even if we do not play any international matches ahead of the Angola clash, we are good to go. We will finalise our tune-ups with local camping, probably from October 1" ; added that the activeness of local-based players in the inaugural National Bank of Malawi (NBM) Women's Premiership will also play a big role in keeping the players in good shape.

a2499.speaker: Lovemore Fazili, Scorchers coach
a2499.speech: Said foreign-based players such as France-based forwards Tabitha Chawinga and Rose Kabzere and free-scoring United States-based striker Temwa Chawinga are expected to join camp at least two weeks before the first match, and believes there will be ample time for the overseas stars to gel with the local-based players during the local camp.

a2499.speaker: Parry Chinyama, football analyst
a2499.speech: Said although the Scorchers recently had some good friendly matches, looking at the period between now and the Angola clash, the absence of another friendly could affect their performance: "Nonetheless, we can rely much on our overseas professionals, who are at the peak of their leagues and have good fitness levels. What Fazili can do is to keep monitoring his players and probably assist in giving tips in the event of not having friendlies."

a2638.speaker: Government officials (Malawi)
a2638.speech: Have already admitted that forex reserves are insufficient, despite the onset of the tobacco season.

a2638.speaker: Illovo (sugar manufacturer)
a2638.speech: Has maintained that its production levels are adequate, yet shop shelves remain empty and prices continue to soar; manufacturers claim there is no shortage.

a3009.speaker: Analysts (unnamed)
a3009.speech: Are wondering whether reciprocity with regard to visa issuing conditions is not open to question.

a3009.speaker: Well-informed observers (unnamed)
a3009.speech: Draw on the unequal balance of power prevailing in international law to call for a thaw, or even for de-escalation, pointing out that reciprocity can only be applied in a diplomatic context of "soft power" and that it must be an instrument of negotiation and of advocacy or lobbying, preserving the interests of the peoples.

a3113.speaker: Zhemu Soda, Zimbabwe’s Mines minister
a3113.speech: In a recent interview with The Financial Gazette, acknowledged the severity of the situation, stating, “The mining industry…”

a3121.speaker: Netumbo Nandi-Ndaitwah, Vice President of Namibia
a3121.speech: Says the government will relay support to ensure that the project succeeds: "Therefore, our government stands firm behind initiatives like the Harambe-Oyetu project. Recognising their pivotal role in food security and job creation through agriculture. Yes, this project, no doubt, though it's now in the hands of the National Youth Council, at its initial stage should still require the support of multiple stakeholders. Of course, our Ministry of Agriculture or the government, through the Ministry of Agriculture, should also continue to give technical support in terms of giving or allowing extension service officers."

a3121.speaker: Netumbo Nandi-Ndaitwah, Vice President of Namibia
a3121.speech: Further stressed the need for regional inhabitants to buy locally fresh produce for project continuity and warned that it would not turn into a white elephant.

a3121.speaker: Marius Sheya, Kunene Governor
a3121.speech: Giving the project overview, said similar projects will be set up in all the constituencies, with plans to also expand the Harambe-Oyetu project to incorporate fish and chicken farming: "When I went to the Roots Project in Stampriet, I said to myself, We will also do something similar in Outjo, in Opuwo in Khorixas, in Kamanjab, and in Okanguati. We will do something similar, and this is just a replica."

a3121.speaker: Zhao Weiping, Chinese Ambassador to Namibia
a3121.speech: Said they sponsored the project because of the China-Namibia Corporation's interest in agricultural development: "I know great efforts are being made by the Namibian government to improve the nation's agricultural sector. As a friend of Namibia, China has always taken what Namibia needs as our priority in implementing development assistance projects in Namibia. Since agriculture is so important to Namibia, we are certainly determined to do more in this area."

a3121.speaker: Dr. Felix Musukubili, project custodian and National Youth Service Commissioner
a3121.speech: Promised the garden would be cultivated to become the bread basket of the town and region.

a3248.speaker: Petteri Taalas, Secretary-General of the World Meteorological Organization
a3248.speech: Said during a press briefing in Geneva that "most of the victims could have been avoided," among other things if the alert had been issued early enough across the whole territory; the WMO had been in contact with the Libyan national meteorological service as early as Sunday 10 September to warn of the arrival of storm Daniel ; also added that most national weather services are not functioning.

a3248.speaker: Libyan Red Crescent
a3248.speech: Declared that 10,000 people were considered missing.

a3248.speaker: Abdul Rahim Maziq, director of the al-Bayda medical centre
International Organization for Migration (IOM)
a3248.speech: According to the IOM, 600,000 migrants, mainly from sub-Saharan Africa, are in Libya.

a3248.speaker: International Organization for Migration (IOM)
a3248.speech: According to the IOM, displaced people in Derna would number 30,000; the IOM added that 6,085 people had been registered as displaced in other areas affected by the storm, notably in Benghazi.

a3248.speaker: Technical committee tasked with assessing the damage, formed by the roads and bridges authority
a3248.speech: Announced that the extent of the collapsed road network in Derna was estimated at 30 kilometres.

a3248.speaker: Martin Griffiths, UN Under-Secretary-General for Humanitarian Affairs and Emergency Relief Coordinator
a3248.speech: Announced an initial allocation of 10 million dollars from the Central Emergency Response Fund (CERF) to support the people affected by the floods.

a3248.speaker: Paris (French government)
a3248.speech: Announced on 12 September the dispatch of a field hospital and 50 people to treat the survivors.

a3329.speaker: Judge Walther Wesser Voltaire, Haitian judge investigating the 2021 assassination of President Jovenel Moise (122-page court document leaked to local media)
a3329.speech: Has charged some fifty people, including the president's widow Martine Moise and former Prime Minister Claude Joseph; alleges that Martine Moise conspired with Claude Joseph to kill the president in order to replace him herself; the judge's order calls for the arrest and trial of those charged.

a3329.speaker: Martine Moise, widow of President Jovenel Moise and former first lady of Haiti
a3329.speech: Did not immediately respond to Reuters' request for comment.

a3329.speaker: Martine Moise, widow of President Jovenel Moise and former first lady of Haiti
a3329.speech: Has criticised on social media what she calls unjust arrests and political persecutions.

a3329.speaker: Claude Joseph, former Prime Minister of Haiti
a3329.speech: Did not immediately respond to Reuters' request for comment.

a3329.speaker: Claude Joseph, former Prime Minister of Haiti
a3329.speech: Told the Miami Herald the president's de-facto successor, Prime Minister Ariel Henry, was the main beneficiary and was now "weaponising the Haitian justice system" to persecute opponents in "a classic coup d'etat."

a3329.speaker: Spokesperson for Prime Minister Ariel Henry's office
a3329.speech: Said the judge was independent and "free to issue his order in accordance with the law and his conscience."

a3329.speaker: Ariel Henry, Prime Minister of Haiti
a3329.speech: Pledged to hold elections but has postponed these indefinitely, citing a devastating earthquake and the growing power of heavily armed criminal gangs, for which he has sought foreign aid.

a3329.speaker: US charges (Miami case)
a3329.speech: The conspirators had, according to US charges, sought to replace Moise with Haitian-American pastor Christian Emmanuel Sanon.

a3431.speaker: African countries / African leaders
a3431.speech: Claim that the United Nations Security Council advances the interests of world powers in an unfair proportion and is outdated; African leaders have been pushing for a permanent seat for their continent on the Security Council for some time.

a3431.speaker: African Union (AU)
a3431.speech: Has called for Africa to have more say in world affairs, claiming this is important as the population, economy, and role of Africa in world politics are on the rise, and that this involves getting more people involved in the process of making policies that affect the whole world.

a3510.speaker: Tedros Adhanom, director-general of the World Health Organisation (WHO)
a3510.speech: Said on the growing gap between the number of vaccines administered in rich countries compared to that in low-income countries.

a3510.speaker: USAID
a3510.speech: According to USAID, wealthy nations are vaccinating one person every second, while only a fifth of the population of low-income countries is expected to be vaccinated by the end of 2021.

a3635.speaker: World Health Organisation (WHO)
a3635.speech: Malaria is a life-threatening disease caused by parasites that are transmitted to people through the bites of infected female Anopheles mosquitoes.

a3635.speaker: World Health Organisation (WHO)
a3635.speech: Recommended the first malaria vaccine in 2021 to prevent the disease in children after the success of the malaria Vaccine Implementation Programme (MVIP) in Ghana and Kenya.

a3635.speaker: National Malaria Elimination Centre (NMEC)
a3635.speech: On average, there are an estimated 20,000 cases of malaria per day in Zambia, and each day, an average of four Zambians die from the disease.

a3635.speaker: Elijah Muchima, Minister of Health of Zambia
a3635.speech: Says Government is working with other cooperating partners and neighbouring countries to end malaria by 2030. "It is the desire of this Government that by 2030 we end malaria. It is our number one agenda in the ministry, working together with other countries because we cannot just deal with it in Zambia. You have also to go to the neighbours collectively."

a3635.speaker: Idah Mumba, community health worker from Mansa district, Luapula Province
a3635.speech: Disclosed that she serves 224 households in her community in providing malaria tests, family planning, and maternal health support. "My coverage community has 987 people. The long distances were my biggest challenge. However, with a bicycle, I can now reach more families and deliver care on time." ; Stressed that early diagnosis and treatment of malaria helps prevent local transmission of the disease and stop the progression of malaria cases from uncomplicated to complicated forms that can be fatal ; thanked Amref for its support in providing a bicycle which has enhanced her service delivery.

a3635.speaker: Anthony Gitau, Johnson and Johnson's director of programme delivery and impact for Africa and the Middle East
a3635.speech: Stressed the importance of investing in community health to deliver universal health coverage (UHC); underscored the urgency of using limited resources efficiently, given the global shortage of six million health workers, two million of whom are community health workers.

a3635.speaker: Landry Dongmo Tsague, Centre for Diseases Control-Africa representative
a3635.speech: Commended CHWs' dedication and emphasised the importance of investing in resilient health systems, particularly after the COVID-19 pandemic; called for mobilisation of domestic resources to be used to train, equip, digitise, and remunerate CHWs in Africa. "We must invest in community health workers as the primary health workforce. We should not consider the CH as a second-class workforce, but rather, as a front-line workforce."

a3635.speaker: World Bicycle Relief
a3635.speech: In Zambia, CHWs equipped with bicycles reported a 63 percent increase in productivity, enabling them to reach more patients and improve maternal and child health outcomes.

a3635.speaker: Maureen Kolenyo, World Bicycle Relief representative
a3635.speech: Detailed the impact of bicycle solutions on CHW productivity, noting that her organisation has distributed over 868,000 bicycles. "Bicycles are affordable, efficient, have low impact on the environment and are easy to use. We have insurmountable evidence to show that they transform health care delivery. A study in Zambia showed a 63 percent increase in service delivery where CHWs had bicycles. That's the power of mobility."

a3635.speaker: Githinji Gitahi, Amref Health Africa group chief executive officer
a3635.speech: Urged African leaders and global stakeholders to rethink health investments to build resilient and sustainable health systems; underlined that Africa's economic and population growth challenges are deeply linked to healthcare financing. "Sub-Saharan Africa is facing an economic crisis, and the lack of fiscal space is a major issue. Investing in health must be tied to population development, ensuring that every girl and woman has the right to make informed reproductive health choices." ; Called for investment shifts towards Primary Health Care (PHC), warning that disproportionate funding for tertiary care leaves millions without access to essential services.

a3635.speaker: Githinji Gitahi, Amref Health Africa group chief executive officer
a3635.speech: Notes that Amref had significant programmes worth about US$28 million in Kenya, Malawi, Zambia, Ethiopia, that were being sponsored by USAID, and that the core of these programmes was around maternal and child health, preventing mother to child HIV transmission. "So, as we speak, we are working with the governments to ensure that no child is going to be exposed to HIV because they were not protected during the mother's pregnancy. That's a risk. We had programmes on HIV prevention testing, for example, we had programmes on what you may call running care treatment centres for HIV, what we call the comprehensive care clinics that have stopped," he said ; said Amref had health workers across Zambia, Malawi, Ethiopia and Kenya, among other countries, that were actively involved in care and treatment for prevention of mother to child HIV and tuberculosis transmission, care and prevention that are out of the health system, though they are still trained.

a3755.speaker: Khumbudzo Ntshavheni, Minister in the Presidency of South Africa
a3755.speech: Announced during a post-Cabinet media briefing on Thursday that South Africa had secured a $115 million emergency funding package from the United States, part of the US President's Emergency Plan for AIDS Relief (PEPFAR) Bridge Plan (PBP), running from 1 October 2025 to 31 March 2026 ; “The PBP is meant to ensure uninterrupted HIV service delivery in South Africa by supporting HIV/AIDS service continuity and prioritising country-specific needs and life-saving impact.”

a3755.speaker: Khumbudzo Ntshavheni, Minister in the Presidency of South Africa
a3755.speech: Emphasized the importance of maintaining momentum toward South Africa's goal of reducing HIV prevalence to 0.1 percent by 2032, and called on both government and international partners to ensure that progress is not reversed ; “We must not regress. We can achieve an HIV-free society later in that period.”

a4285.speaker: The Investigator Magazine (exclusive investigation)
a4285.speech: Reveals that the Malawian government, under President Lazarus Chakwera’s administration, is illegally transferring the private biometric data of its citizens to a foreign company in India for passport printing ; has also uncovered that the data of Malawian citizens is being sent to India for the printing process, a direct violation of Malawi’s newly enacted data protection laws.

a4285.speaker: The Investigator Magazine (reporters’ field visits)
a4285.speech: Our reporters visited key Immigration offices in Blantyre, Lilongwe, Mzuzu, and Mangochi. In all locations, there was no evidence of active passport printing. The only passports observed were a few samples being tested in Lilongwe, confirming that the entire production process has been moved offshore.

a4285.speaker: President Lazarus Chakwera and his administration
a4285.speech: In March of last year, claimed a “cyber-attack” had compromised the national passport system, halting all local production.

a4285.speaker: Sources within the government and the ruling Malawi Congress Party (MCP)
a4285.speech: Suggest the disruption was a manufactured crisis, stemming from an internal power struggle over a lucrative printing contract.

a4285.speaker: Ezekiel Ching’oma, Malawi Homeland Security Minister
a4285.speech: Announced a “breakthrough,” presenting a batch of just 5,000 passports as proof that production had resumed.

a4285.speaker: Malawi government
a4285.speech: Claimed that MSP would be printing 15,000 passports per day — a claim directly contradicted by the limited number of passports that have been received in Malawi ; has offered no explanation as to why a local solution was not pursued or why the national data protection laws were bypassed.

a4285.speaker: Homeland Security Ministry and Immigration Department (non-response)
a4285.speech: Are yet to dispute the claims.

a4400.speaker: Governor of Upper Nile State (James Odhok)
a4400.speech: Disclosed that the suspension of U.S. foreign assistance has affected many humanitarian organizations serving internally displaced persons, returnees, and refugees in the area ; stated that most activities of non-governmental organizations in the transit center in Renk and other camps have stopped due to a lack of funding, and that organizations that rely on USAID funding have been impacted, prompting them to halt some of their operations ; added that the state government and the aid agencies are trying to utilize the minimum resources to transport and resettle the displaced: "We have taken the necessary precautions. However, some decisions by the American president have halted the operations of certain organizations working in the area, but we are working diligently" ; said the transportation capacity for refugees and returnees from the border state onward to Juba and other states has been remarkably reduced: "Currently, refugees are being transported, but not as before when one or two planes would arrive daily. Now, the International Organization for Migration provides one plane daily, and others are transported by riverboats, sometimes more than three times a day." ; "Some organizations that receive support from America, such as World Vision and others, have ceased their activities due to a lack of funding, while others continue their operations."

a4400.speaker: UN agencies
a4400.speech: Say more than one million people have poured into South Sudan from war-torn Sudan since April 2023, setting a new record in the ongoing humanitarian and displacement crisis ignited by nearly two years of fighting.

a4400.speaker: International Organization for Migration (IOM) and UN Refugee Agency (UNHCR) (published data)
a4400.speech: According to data published by IOM and UNHCR, the highest influx of more than 770,200 entered through the Joda border point in Renk County in Upper Nile.

a4553.speaker: Godswill Akpabio, Senate President of Nigeria
a4553.speech: Announced during plenary on Wednesday that the service chiefs would appear before the lawmakers next week, confirming that the security chiefs had communicated their readiness for the engagement. “In the chambers last week we invited our service chiefs to come for a closed door briefing on the general security of the nation and they sent a message to me that they will be ready in a week. So, I will expect them, we will take them latest next week.”

a4553.speaker: Nigeria's security chiefs
a4553.speech: Sent a message to the Senate President saying they would be ready for the closed-door briefing in a week.

a4553.speaker: National Bureau of Statistics (NBS) report
a4553.speech: Recently revealed that insecurity in Nigeria claimed over 600,000 lives between May 2023 and April 2024; the report also showed that 2,235,954 Nigerians were kidnapped and ₦2.23 trillion (approximately $1.44 billion) paid in ransom during the period.

a4553.speaker: Scott Perry, US Congressman
a4553.speech: Alleged that the United States Agency for International Development (USAID) had provided funding to terrorist organisations, including ISIS, al-Qaeda and Boko Haram, in Nigeria.

a4656.speaker: Pascal Essou, Ombudsman (Médiateur) of the Republic of Benin
a4656.speech: “Our action is part of a perspective of pushing back the barriers of intolerance and radicalization, and of contributing durably to peace, social cohesion and living together within our communities”; he recalled that, beyond its traditional missions of improving the rule of law and administrative governance, his institution also works to promote political and socio-community dialogue.

a4656.speaker: Djibril Mama Cissé, Prefect of Borgou (speaking for his colleagues of Alibori, Donga and Atacora)
a4656.speech: praised the relevance of the project, in a context where the rise of violent extremism, with its corollaries of radicalism and terrorism, constitutes a serious threat to peace in certain departments of the north, where young people may be led to become the object of all sorts of temptations.

a4656.speaker: Simplice Kouassi, representative of the USAID regional director
a4656.speech: said the project falls within a series of activities of the Regional Coastal Countries Support Program (PRAPC) that will enable young people to effectively and constructively carry the concerns of their communities to the public authorities and national institutions, while demonstrating the positive role they play within their communities.

a4656.speaker: Boukari Bagnan, representative of the youth of North Benin
a4656.speech: “Give us more tools and opportunities to optimize our civic engagement”; he expressed the commitment of the young people of the north to work toward the accomplishment of the mission assigned to them within the framework of the implementation of the project, promising to be the builders of a lasting peace.

a4698.speaker: Bola Tinubu, President of Nigeria
a4698.speech: Welcomed Petrobras’s imminent return to Nigeria and said at a joint press conference in Brasília that Petrobras’ return would reignite economic cooperation in the energy sector between the two countries ; “We have the largest gas repository. So I don’t see why Petrobras doesn’t join as a partner in Nigeria as soon as possible. I appreciate President Lula’s promise that this will be done as soon as possible.”

a4698.speaker: Bola Tinubu, President of Nigeria
a4698.speech: Praised President Lula’s commitment to revitalising the partnership between the two countries, noting that Nigeria’s economic space remains a virgin land, full of opportunities for Brazilian companies ; acknowledged Embraer’s efforts in addressing the critical challenges of local airline operations in Nigeria, primarily through establishing a Service Centre ; recalled his previous engagements in Brazil and emphasised the urgency of moving beyond symbolic ties to concrete economic cooperation ; “Honourable Ministers of both countries, members of the Brazil Business Group, I have listened carefully to my friend, President Lula. We had a lengthy discussion. We talked about history and about African and Brazilian heritage. We tried to see why we are not at the level we wanted. We have allowed some problems and activities in the past to deter us from making progress and fulfilling our promises. But today we say that is the end of that. This is my third visit to the country. First, the visit to attend the G20. Second, on climate change, BRICS. And today, an official and state visit was very emotional.”

a4698.speaker: Bola Tinubu, President of Nigeria
a4698.speech: Underscored Nigeria’s readiness to partner with Brazil on technology transfer, food security, manufacturing, and renewable energy ; “Today, we are fighting and working hard to bring our sovereignty to the level of expectation that we as a nation, the most populous, the most dynamic country, Nigeria, share with Brazil. We need to share—technology transfer, energy, economy—so that Brazil can continue to widen the opportunities for us to embrace Africa. Africa is the new frontier. There is no other way to do it than to embrace it with technology, fast development, research, food sovereignty, and manufacturing.”

a4698.speaker: Bola Tinubu, President of Nigeria
a4698.speech: Stressed the need for investment and knowledge exchange on healthcare and pharmaceuticals: “We have elevated this promise to the path of reality, as you have seen in various MOUs. I don’t know why the manufacturing of generic drugs, which Brazil has done deeply and far, cannot be in Nigeria. I don’t see why the technological superiority of Brazil is not shared with Africa. We assured each other that only we can develop our economies to help our sovereignty.”

a4698.speaker: Bola Tinubu, President of Nigeria
a4698.speech: Assured investors that Nigeria’s economic reforms are yielding results: “The reforms I’ve embarked upon since I took over in Nigeria have been very impactful. It was initially painful, but today the result is blossoming. It’s getting clearer to the people. We have more money for the economy, and there will be no more corruption. We have the governor of the Central Bank of Nigeria here. You don’t have to know him before getting the foreign exchange you need. The speculators are out. In our currency market, the door is open for businesses.”

a4698.speaker: Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, President of Brazil
a4698.speech: Welcomed the restart of the Brazil-Nigeria relationship: “At a time when protectionism and unilateralism have returned, Nigeria and Brazil reaffirm their bet on free trade and productive integration. We continue to be dedicated to building a world of peace, free from hegemonic impositions. There are many possibilities for synergy between the world’s two largest countries with Black populations. Agriculture and livestock, oil and gas, fertilisers, aircraft, and machinery, among others, represent wide avenues for cooperation.”

a4698.speaker: Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, President of Brazil
a4698.speech: Spoke further on the BASA agreement: “Increasing the direct connections between Nigeria and Brazil is another essential step to strengthen the ties between our societies. We have approved the launch of a direct flight, to be operated by Nigeria’s largest airline company, Air Peace, between Lagos and São Paulo.”

a4955.speaker: Published financial results of Sunbird Tourism plc and Blantyre Hotels plc (BHL)
a4955.speech: Show that although the two Malawi Stock Exchange-listed hospitality firms posted profits, revenue was subdued due to challenging economic conditions.

a4955.speaker: Sunbird Tourism plc (published half-year results)
a4955.speech: Indicated that US government changes in international aid, particularly the closure of USaid, affected demand while high interest and inflation rates raised operating costs by 33 percent to K12.5 billion. Reads part of the results: "Locally, the hospitality sector was also heavily affected by changes in the US government policy on international aid." ; "In addition, the economic environment for the reporting period continued to be challenging characterised by high interest rates, shortage of foreign currency and high inflation particularly the food inflation, which drove up the hotel's operating costs and also affected demand for the hotels products and services."

a4955.speaker: Malawi Government Annual Economic Report 2025
a4955.speech: Reports that the sector added 70,000 jobs, registered K62.7 billion in investments and contributed 6.7 percent to the country's gross domestic product (GDP); shows the sector's contribution to GDP more than doubled in 2024 at K865.2 billion from K394.7 billion during the pandemic period in 2020.

a4955.speaker: Memory Kamthunzi, Malawi Tourism Council executive director
a4955.speech: Said the tourism sector has shown strong signs of recovery, reflected in the significant increase in its contribution to GDP and job creation: "This indicates resilience and renewed investor confidence and the rise in employment figures highlights the sector's role in economic revitalisation." ; "However, this recovery has not been uniform across all tourism-related businesses." ; said while major hospitality establishments, airlines and tour operators have rebounded well, many small and medium enterprises, which form the backbone of the sector, are still struggling with financial constraints, low capacity utilisation and operational challenges.

a4955.speaker: Innocent Kaliati, managing director of Orbis Destination Management Company
a4955.speech: Said although tourist figures surpassed the pre-pandemic period at 1.1 million in 2024 from 960,000 in 2019, the post-pandemic recovery remains slow: "From my perspective, tourism in Malawi has been a rising graph since Covid. It is slow, but it is rising. We are seeing more tourists coming in and the latest statistics show we managed 1.1 million visitors in 2024." ; "I also feel Malawi can do better by targeting new markets to supplement the existing ones."

a4955.speaker: Brian Kampanje, financial expert
a4955.speech: Said the performance is better considering the acute inflationary macroeconomic environment, but urged the players to be innovative to ensure resilience going ahead: "While the impact of the closure of significant USaid programmes in Malawi's hospitality industry is not known, the resilience of the sector has been quite good." ; "It is also an opportunity for the sector to be more innovative."

a5039.speaker: United Arab Emirates (government)
a5039.speech: Said it would triple renewable energy production as part of a raft of environmental initiatives announced on Monday, and unveiled national strategies on hydrogen and electric cars.

a5039.speaker: Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum, UAE Prime Minister and ruler of Dubai
a5039.speech: Said after a cabinet meeting that ministers approved an "updated national energy strategy" that aims to "triple the contribution of renewable energy over the next seven years" ; said in a statement that up to 200 billion dirhams ($54 billion) will be invested over the same period to meet growing electricity demand ; said another initiative "aims to consolidate the country's position as a producer and exporter of low-emission hydrogen over the next eight years" by developing supply chains and infrastructure and setting up a research and development centre ; the statement added that Chinese-based WeRide will receive the country's first national licence for self-driving cars.

a5039.speaker: Climate activists
a5039.speech: Have criticised the UAE's hosting of the November-December COP negotiations, questioning whether one of the world's biggest oil producers should have such a key role in the fight against global warming.

a5039.speaker: United Arab Emirates (government)
a5039.speech: Argues that oil remains indispensable to the global economy and is pushing the merits of carbon capture ; said in 2021, ahead of COP26 in Glasgow, that it was targeting net zero domestic carbon emissions by 2050.

a5096.speaker: Government of Malawi
a5096.speech: has hailed the upward trend in mining revenue as evidence of progress in its efforts to transform the sector into a pillar of economic growth.

a5112.speaker: Energy and Water Utilities Regulatory Authority (EWURA)
a5112.speech: Announced the new cap prices on Tuesday - a 36/- and 23/- reduction in cap prices for petroleum and diesel respectively.

a5112.speaker: Dr James Andilile, EWURA Director General (statement)
a5112.speech: According to a statement, the reductions are driven by declines in FOB prices - down 0.2 per cent for petrol, 5.5 per cent for diesel and 3.5 per cent for kerosene - coupled with 3.96 per cent depreciation in the applicable exchange rate for the period ; according to the statement, prices at the Port of Mtwara remain unchanged, while the Port of Tanga has seen a notable decrease of 12.66 per cent for both petrol and diesel.

a5112.speaker: Energy and Water Utilities Regulatory Authority (EWURA) (directive)
a5112.speech: Has issued a directive reminding all retailers and wholesalers to adhere strictly to the stipulated fuel prices, warning that legal action will be taken against non-compliance.

a5222.speaker: Office of the National Security Adviser (Nuhu Ribadu), press statement signed by Zakari U. Mijinyawa, Head of Strategic Communication
a5222.speech: confirmed the escape of one of the detained executives of Binance, Nadeem Anjarwalla, from custody; said the suspect flew out of the country with a smuggled passport; said that after being briefed on what had happened, it took urgent action to apprehend the suspect, working with relevant security agencies, MDAs, and the international community; added that security services are working with Interpol to get an international arrest warrant for the suspect. “The personnel responsible for the custody of the suspect have been arrested, and a thorough investigation is ongoing to unravel the circumstances that led to his escape from lawful detention. Recall that the Federal Government of Nigeria, like other governments around the world, has been investigating money laundering and terrorism financing transactions perpetrated on the Binance currency exchange platform. Until his escape, Nadeem Anjarwalla, who holds British and Kenyan nationalities and serving as Binance’s Africa regional manager, was being tried by Nigerian courts. The suspect escaped while under a 14-day remand order by a court in Nigeria. He was scheduled to appear before the court again on 4 April 2024. We urge the Nigerian public and the international community to provide whatever information they have that can assist law enforcement agencies to apprehend the suspect.”

a5222.speaker: Nigerian court (ruling reported by SaharaReporters)
a5222.speech: said Anjarwalla and his colleague, Tigran Gambaryan, should remain in detention for at least two more weeks in Nigeria after appearing in court last week even though they had not been charged with a crime.

a5234.speaker: Premier Bank (press release)
a5234.speech: "Premier Bank is proud to announce the launch of its enhanced direct SWIFT payment platform, transforming international money transfers by enabling businesses and individuals in the country to send and receive funds globally — faster, simpler, and more secure than ever before." ; said the upgrade replaces the long-standing hassles that slowed cross-border transactions for over two decades, and that customers can seamlessly transact in major global currencies, eliminating previous currency limitations that hindered the country's importers and exporters ; said Premier Bank aims to accelerate trade, stimulate economic growth, and support the country's strategic integration into regional and global markets, and that this latest advancement reinforces its leadership role in fostering a robust and inclusive financial ecosystem.

a5254.speaker: Latest second quarterly reports (Eswatini government)
a5254.speech: According to the latest second quarterly reports, government, through its initiatives and partnering with the private sector, jointly created more than 3 500 jobs in the past three months.

a5254.speaker: Ministry of Public Service of Eswatini (quarterly report)
a5254.speech: Reported that it issued authorities for the Ministry of Education and Training to fill vacant posts, including legal advisor and legal officer (TSC), head teacher and deputy head teacher, inspector of schools and teacher posts ; reported that between July 1, 2025 and September 30 it granted authority to the Ministry of Tinkhundla Administration and Development to fill the vacant position of community development officer ; granted authority for a waiver to the Treasury and Stores Department to fill vacant positions of one financial controller, two principal accountants and two accountant posts, and a waiver for the redeployment of three heavy duty drivers ; issued authority to the Ministry of Economic Planning and Development (Central Statistical Office) to engage staff on temporary terms for the 2027 Population and Housing Census, the 2025/26 Economic Statistics Survey and to extend the engagement of staff for the Eswatini Annual Agricultural Survey 2025/2026 ; granted authority to the Ministry of Health to fill permanent posts for the Renal Dialysis Unit, renew a warehouse assistant contract at the Central Medical Stores, create posts for the new health facility organisational structure, engage 72 spray operators, fill newly-created pharmacy cadre positions, and hire a cleaning and hygiene services provider.

a5254.speaker: Ministry of Labour and Social Security of Eswatini (quarterly report)
a5254.speech: Reported that during the quarter under review a total of 16 redundancies were reported, affecting 2 056 employees, compared to six redundancies involving 133 employees in 2024 and 14 redundancies affecting 1 072 employees in 2023, indicating a 63 per cent increase in reported retrenchments ; reported that the sudden surge in redundancies is a result of the United States Presidential Order reducing funding to member states under the PEPFAR Project ; "During the second quarter of 2025, the unregulated (Other) sector recorded the highest proportion of redundancies at 31 per cent, with a total of 171 employees affected. The textiles and apparel sector, although recording only two cases of redundancies, accounted for the highest number of affected employees - 572 in total, representing 28 per cent of all retrenched employees" ; reported that the security sector also recorded two cases of redundancies and ranked second highest with 560 employees affected, the mining and quarrying sector third with 436 employees affected, and the wholesale, retail and distributive trade sector with three cases affecting 202 employees.

a5309.speaker: National Institute of Statistics and Demography of Benin (Instad) (quarterly foreign trade statistics bulletin)
a5309.speech: According to the bulletin, the second quarter of 2024 shows a decline in exports and imports: merchandise exports fell 12.9% from the first quarter, driven by "oilcake and other solid residues..." (-7.6 percentage points), "petroleum oils or oils obtained from bituminous minerals (other than crude) and preparations..." (-3.0 points) and "edible nuts..." (-2.7 points), while year-on-year foreign sales rose 25.6%, led by "cotton (excluding linters), neither carded nor combed" (+11.5 points) and "oilcake and other solid residues..." (+9.8 points); merchandise imports fell 13.2% quarter-on-quarter, driven by "fertilizers, n.e.s." (-3.7 points), "herbicides, anti-sprouting products and plant-growth regulators..." (-3.1 points) and "mineral or chemical nitrogenous fertilizers" (-2.9 points), and fell 27.7% year-on-year, which Instad explains by a drop in imports of petroleum oils (-4.7 points), phosphatic fertilizers (-3.0 points) and palm oil and its fractions (-2.7 points).

a5309.speaker: National Institute of Statistics and Demography of Benin (Instad)
a5309.speech: Noted that the dynamics of Benin's external trade are marked by strong seasonal variations, with the evolution of the various external trade series characterised by seasonal phenomena; over the last four quarters Benin's exports followed a very irregular path, seasonally adjusted foreign sales standing at 179.0 billion CFA francs in the first quarter of 2024 against 141.1 billion a year earlier (up 26.9%), while seasonally adjusted purchases abroad fell 27.6% year-on-year to 461.1 billion CFA francs.

a5338.speaker: Proplastics
a5338.speech: Says the increase to 30 percent of export proceeds surrender requirements to the Reserve Bank of Zimbabwe (RBZ) beginning of this year has rendered its export business uncompetitive.

a5346.speaker: 2021 Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) report
a5346.speech: According to it, climate change is unequivocally a man-made phenomenon.

a5346.speaker: International Energy Association (IEA), Net Zero by 2050 report
a5346.speech: Noted that hard-to-abate sectors - like cement, steel and chemicals, road trucking, container shipping, and aviation - will need green hydrogen if the world is to remain on course to achieve climate neutrality by 2050.

a5383.speaker: Ibrahim Traoré, military doctor and president of the special delegation of Commune IV
a5383.speech: took the floor to salute this fine initiative and this surge of solidarity towards the disadvantaged: “We sincerely thank the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia for this gesture, which comes at just the right time. It is in difficult moments that one recognises one's friends. And Saudi Arabia has just proven it to us through this donation of food baskets.”

a5383.speaker: A. Cheick Ibrahim Kontao, director of the NGO Al Farouk-Mali
a5383.speech: addressed the audience with religious exhortations: “Those who spend their wealth in the path of God are like a grain that sprouts seven ears, in each ear there are a hundred grains. God multiplies blessings for whom He wills. God is great and wise.” ; recalled the saying of Muhammad, son of Abdallah: “Whoever relieves a Muslim of a hardship of this world, God will relieve him of a hardship on the Day of Resurrection.”

a5383.speaker: A. Cheick Ibrahim Kontao, director of the NGO Al Farouk-Mali
a5383.speech: said of the response to the floods: “the State was among the first to intervene in order to alleviate the suffering of the victims by providing precious resources and by calling on its partners to collaborate. In response to this appeal, the NGO Al Farouk mobilised its partners. By the Grace of God, the King Salman Centre for Relief and Humanitarian Aid stood by our side, adopting a brotherly approach and always on the front line of this humanitarian mission, with kindness and compassion. Today, we celebrate together the launch of a project to assist several families in Bamako, Koulikoro, Segou and Mopti.” ; said each food kit is made up of 25 kg of rice, 10 kg of noodles, 5 kg of sugar and 5 litres of oil.

a5383.speaker: A. Cheick Ibrahim Kontao, director of the NGO Al Farouk-Mali
a5383.speech: expressed, on behalf of the NGO Al Farouk, his deep gratitude to King Salman bin Abdulaziz and Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman for this important donation: “I also wish to thank the team of the King Salman Centre for Relief and Humanitarian Aid, led by Dr. Rabia and his collaborators, in particular our brothers who travelled long distances to Mali to serve their brothers in God, for their remarkable efforts aimed at promoting security, stability and well-being throughout the world and particularly in the Islamic world. I also thank His Excellency the Ambassador of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia and all the members of the embassy for their availability and their contribution to our country. I cannot conclude without expressing my gratitude to the government of Mali, under the leadership of the President of the Transition, General Assimi Goïta, for all the facilities granted to the Al Farouk organisation so that it may carry out its mission. I pray to God to grant them success in leading this country towards a serene future.”

a5383.speaker: Abdullah Saleh Saber, Ambassador of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia to Mali
a5383.speech: saluted the fraternal and historic relations between the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia and the sister Republic of Mali in various fields, in confirmation of the Kingdom's willingness to stand by the brotherly Malian people ; “I thank the government of the Custodian of the Two Holy Mosques for the humanitarian aid it provides. I also cannot fail to thank the King Salman Humanitarian Aid and Relief Centre for its efforts in the area of food aid. I also thank the Minister-Commissioner for Food Security for the efforts and the cooperation you have deployed to implement this programme, and my thanks go to the highest authorities for all the facilities that have been provided to us.” ; thanked the NGO Al-Farouk for its valuable efforts in organising this launch ceremony.

a5383.speaker: Redouwane Ag Mohamed Ali, Minister-Commissioner for Food Security of Mali
a5383.speech: saluted all the actors who contributed to the realisation of this purely humanitarian action: “It is with great satisfaction that I note the completion of a project on which we worked with the NGO Al-Farouk. We involved the governors of the regions concerned, namely the district of Bamako and the regions of Koulikoro, Ségou and Mopti, to produce the lists of all the beneficiaries, with eligibility criteria that were determined by common agreement with the NGO Al Farouk and its partners. Thank you to each and every one for the completion of this noble action; it is never a happy thing to see fellow citizens in need of assistance. We must all work together to create living conditions worthy of our fellow citizens in situations of food difficulty.”

a5383.speaker: Beneficiaries of the food kits
a5383.speech: did not stop thanking King Salman and Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman for this generous donation.

a5414.speaker: Salomon April, Hardap Governor
a5414.speech: Highlighted the significance of this year’s International Women’s Day, coinciding with the election of Netumbo Nandi-Ndaitwah as Swapo’s first female president, speaking at the Women’s Day celebration in Stampriet Village.

a5414.speaker: Woita Kapumburu, Acting Director of Health and Social Services in Kavango East Region
a5414.speech: Said limited resources and poverty among people in rural areas are hampering efforts to end the spread of HIV/AIDS in Namibia, at the World AIDS Day Commemoration at Rundu.

a5427.speaker: Chaba Mokuku, CAFI Project Manager
a5427.speech: Explained that the project, which falls under the Ministry of Trade and is supported by the World Bank, aims to accelerate the implementation of key government policies ; highlighted the project’s collaboration with multiple government ministries and institutions, including the Ministry of Agriculture and Food Security, the Ministry of Finance and Development with the Revenue Services Lesotho, the Central Bank of Lesotho, and the Ministry of Local Government, Chieftaincy, Home Affairs, and Police through the Maseru City Council (MCC) ; emphasised that CAFI is anchored on three main pillars: improving the business environment, supporting entrepreneurship and MSMEs, and reviving the textile and horticulture industries ; “The project aligns with the National Strategic Development Plan (NSDP II), which runs until 2027. Its first key performance area is promoting inclusive and sustainable economic growth. Through CAFI, we are targeting priority sectors including manufacturing, agriculture, tourism, technology, the creative industry, and innovation.”

a5427.speaker: Mamoriti Phangoa, acting LEHSFF Manager
a5427.speech: According to her, the hub has trained and supported 15 Entrepreneurship Support Organisations (ESOs), incubated up to 500 entrepreneurs with access to business tools and mentorship, invested in 50 innovative SMEs and startups, and launched one Venture Capital (VC) seed fund to finance promising new businesses, creating a total of 1250 permanent and temporary jobs ; added that LEHSFF is also strengthening Lesotho’s regional entrepreneurship ecosystem and tapping into the Diaspora’s expertise and resources, and that the hub aims to develop a five-year strategic plan to ensure sustainability and long-term impact beyond the lifespan of the CAFI project.

a5427.speaker: Lehlohonolo Chefa, LEAP Manager
a5427.speech: Explained that the Matching Grant Scheme is designed to strengthen small businesses while ensuring funds are directed toward impactful development rather than recurring costs ; “LEAP does not provide cash directly to businesses; instead, it purchases or secures the necessary resources on behalf of entrepreneurs. These restrictions ensure funds are channelled into sustainable, long-term improvements.”

a5427.speaker: Thabiso Kolotsana, journalist
a5427.speech: Emphasised the importance of regular CAFI media engagements: “Workshops like this are vital in spreading educational information to the public. LEAP, in particular, is one of the most important programmes I’ve learned about — it was my first time hearing about it.”

a5552.speaker: The columnist (Business Unpacked, June 21 2022 entry 'Why devaluation may have been a misdiagnosis')
a5552.speech: Submitted that while devaluation is a common monetary policy tool used by countries with either fixed or semi-fixed exchange rates, it may not be the magic wand Malawi needed.

a5552.speaker: Bingu wa Mutharika, former President of Malawi
a5552.speech: Stood his ground between 2010 and 2012 against International Monetary Fund recommendations to devalue the kwacha; his argument was premised on the fact that the move would hurt local consumers and only benefit importers more as Malawi was a predominantly importing and consuming economy with negligible exports.

a5552.speaker: McDonald Mafuta-Mwale (PhD), Reserve Bank of Malawi Governor
a5552.speech: Made a bold statement that this time around "the patient", Malawi, has decided to ignore what "the doctor", IMF, has prescribed: "We have made it clear to the IMF that we have had a lot of devaluations without achieving the intended result and we cannot repeat that because it only hurts our people with inflation. Our emphasis is now on the enhancement of foreign exchange supply through local production and exportation, incentivising both local and foreign investors, and seeking other donors to assist Malawi as we develop our own capacity to generate export proceeds."

a5552.speaker: Economists Thomas Chataghalala Munthali and Frank Ngalande, in a paper titled 'Is devaluation an option for Malawi's current debt challenge'
a5552.speech: Cautioned that devaluation should not be the path to take because that would cause more harm than good.

a5605.speaker: Save the Children
a5605.speech: said about 1.12 billion children globally, or 48 percent of children worldwide, are unable to afford a balanced diet, releasing new data on the eve of the Nutrition for Growth (N4G) summit in Paris ; said hikes in food prices combined with the increasing cost of living around the world has forced millions of families to eat less adequate, less balanced and less diverse food, putting child development and wellbeing at risk ; analysed the cost of a healthy diet in 167 countries and found that nearly half of the children in these countries are in families that can't afford these basics in their communities, with more than two in every three children (68 percent) in low- and lower-middle income countries unable to afford a healthy diet ; said the relatively high cost of nutritious foods is one of the greatest obstacles to giving children a healthy diet.

a5605.speaker: Mayra Alejandra Obregon Ocoro, 29, national Youth Coordinator for the Scaling Up Nutrition Civil Society Movement (SUN CSN), Colombia
a5605.speech: “The situation faced by nearly half of the world’s children who cannot afford a balanced diet is alarming and reflects a global food crisis that we cannot ignore. In Colombia, a country with deep social inequalities, many children and young people suffer from malnutrition and do not have access to adequate food. Poverty and rising food prices have led families to prioritize quantity over quality, resulting in diets high in carbohydrates and poor in essential nutrients. It is critical that leaders attending the N4G summit commit to taking concrete and sustainable actions. I hope they will focus on implementing policies that reduce the cost of healthy food, promote local agriculture, and ensure equitable distribution of resources.”

a5605.speaker: Sohanur Rahman, 28, national Youth Coordinator for the Scaling Up Nutrition Civil Society Movement, Bangladesh
a5605.speech: “In my country Bangladesh, I have seen firsthand how rising food prices, economic inequality, and climate-induced disasters including extreme weather events like floods push families into food insecurity, forcing children to rely on cheap, nutrient-poor diets. At the N4G summit in Paris, leaders must commit to transformative policies that make nutritious food affordable and accessible for all. This includes strengthening social protection programs, supporting small-scale farmers, and investing in climate-resilient agriculture to safeguard food security against climate disasters.”

a5605.speaker: Hannah Stephenson, Save the Children’s Global Nutrition Lead
a5605.speech: “The N4G summit is a critical opportunity for the international community to drive progress against malnutrition, putting nutrition at the center of a sustainable development agenda – which in a world where aid cuts are becoming the norm, is more crucial than ever. Healthy diets play a critical role in the prevention of malnutrition, which can have life-long consequences for children. However, they can also be less affordable than unhealthy diets, with globally, nearly half of the world’s children unable to afford a balanced diet. There is an urgent need for collective action to address malnutrition in all its forms—. The health and well-being of millions of children depend on our sustained efforts.”

a5605.speaker: Save the Children
a5605.speech: is calling on leaders at the N4G Summit in Paris to strengthen the transition towards sustainable food systems, promote equitable access to nutritious diets, strengthen health systems to make them resilient and increase universal health coverage, strengthen social protection systems and leave no one behind, and empower women while placing them at the heart of nutrition ; “We call on leaders to commit to integrating nutrition outcomes into a wide range of sectors including environment and climate. By prioritising evidence-based policies, increasing financial commitments, and fostering multi-sectoral collaboration, only then can we drive meaningful progress toward ending malnutrition.”

a5651.speaker: White House
a5651.speech: Announced on Friday that US President Donald Trump cancelled $4.9 billion of congressionally approved foreign aid funding, adding that the president would “put AMERICA FIRST!” ; Said Trump has a “solid legal basis” for the maneuver.

a5651.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a5651.speech: In a letter, informed House of Representatives Speaker Mike Johnson that funding would be withheld for 15 international programs.

a5651.speaker: Democratic Party lawmakers opposed to the foreign aid cuts
a5651.speech: Said Trump's decision raises the likelihood of a federal shutdown later in the year; said attempts to reverse funding that has previously been approved by Congress would destroy negotiations within the legislative body later in the year.

a5651.speaker: Susan Collins, Republican Senator of Maine and chair of the Senate Appropriations Committee
a5651.speech: Called Trump's move illegal: “Instead of this attempt to undermine the law, the appropriate way is to identify ways to reduce excessive spending” ; “Any effort to rescind appropriated funds without congressional approval is a clear violation of the law.”

a5651.speaker: Chuck Schumer, leader of the Democratic minority in the US Senate
a5651.speech: “It's clear neither Trump nor Congressional Republicans have any plan to avoid a painful and entirely unnecessary shutdown.”

a5651.speaker: Stephane Dujarric, United Nations spokesperson
a5651.speech: “This is going to make our budget situation or liquidity situation that much more challenging.”

a5870.speaker: Rodolphe, manager of Le Niveau, a second-hand goods shop in Cotonou
a5870.speech: "I set up here nearly eight years ago. I spent ten years in the second-hand clothing market before that."

a5870.speaker: National Institute of Statistics and Demography (Benin)
a5870.speech: According to the Institute, between 2020 and 2022 exports in the second-hand clothing sector tripled in the country, from a little over 804 million CFA francs to 2,493 million francs, while over the same period imports exceeded 40,000 million francs.

a5870.speaker: Rodolphe, manager of Le Niveau, a second-hand goods shop in Cotonou
a5870.speech: "Most come from England, Germany, Switzerland, Belgium" ; "In France, they use them too much" ; "Sometimes I go to Lome to look, because in Benin the stuff doesn't come out the way it should. And then, there are things that are too worn, whereas in Togo or Ghana it is still in good condition. There are unsold items, end-of-series items" ; says he targets as a priority "the three nearby countries [Togo, Ghana and Nigeria] where transport will not cost too much."
