a5870.speaker: Georges Mensah, vendor for fifteen years at the Missebo second-hand clothing market
a5870.speech: Sources his goods in Turkey and China; the merchandise takes two to three weeks to arrive by boat, and for a 500-kilo bag he pays a customs duty of 30,000 euros, an operation he repeats "two to three times" a year ; "They often come from Cote d'Ivoire, Nigeria, Mali, and Equatorial Guinea" ; assures that "Nigeriens come and pay a lot here, even Cote d'Ivoire" ; says he "started out under the sun, by the roadside."

a5870.speaker: Godfroyd, a 25-year-old customer
a5870.speech: "It's a good deal for me; if I had to go and buy these things in a shop it would be double."

a5935.speaker: Supreme Court Chief Justice John Roberts (court order)
a5935.speech: Issued an order halting a lower court ruling that required the Trump administration to release some $2 billion in foreign aid, independently intervening to suspend Ali's ruling, and set a deadline of Friday 12 noon for the State Department and USAID contractors to respond to the Trump administration request.

a5935.speaker: US District Judge Amir Ali (court order)
a5935.speech: Had previously set a firm deadline of 11.59 pm Wednesday for the State Department and USAID to settle outstanding payments with contractors for work completed before Feb. 13 ; earlier this month issued a temporary restraining order preventing the Trump administration from freezing foreign aid funds during ongoing proceedings, and approved the plaintiffs' request to implement his previous order, giving the State Department and USAID a 36-hour deadline for the payment.

a5935.speaker: CBS News
a5935.speech: Reported that the Trump administration took the case to the Supreme Court, seeking intervention to block the release of the frozen foreign aid funds.

a5935.speaker: Sarah Harris, acting Solicitor General
a5935.speech: Argued that Ali's order affects roughly $2 billion and criticized his Wednesday night deadline, saying that it “moved the goalposts” ; wrote that the order does not align with any actual payment deadlines related to respondents' invoices, drawdown requests, or any other obligations ; said officials at the “highest levels of government” are handling the issue and informed the Supreme Court that the Trump administration is “undertaking substantial efforts to review payment requests and release payments” ; said the district court's payment deadline “makes full compliance impossible” and clarified that resuming funding for canceled or suspended contracts requires multiple steps, involving various agencies and extensive documentation ; called for an administrative stay to preserve the status quo, arguing that it would prevent agencies from being placed in the position of “violating a federal court order requiring payments on thousands of requests within a 30-some-hour deadline, despite their efforts,” while the court examines the validity of their challenge.

a5935.speaker: US Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia Circuit (ruling)
a5935.speech: Rejected the administration's bid, ruling that Judge Ali's orders were not subject to appeal.

a5935.speaker: The plaintiffs (companies, nonprofits and organizations relying on State Department and USAID funding)
a5935.speech: Told Ali that, despite his order, they still had not received foreign aid funds and needed immediate payment for their work.

a5935.speaker: Peter Marocco, director of foreign assistance at the State Department (declaration)
a5935.speech: Said in a declaration earlier this month that the administration is doing an “individualized review” of contracts and grants, calling the process “cumbersome” and requiring multiple steps ; estimated that USAID must pay at least “$1.5 billion” across 2,000 requests, while the State Department owes “$400 million” ; warned these payments “cannot be accomplished in the time allotted by the Court” and would take weeks instead.

a5994.speaker: Emmanuel Macron, President of the French Republic
a5994.speech: Made a point of reminding Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu that his country had been created thanks to the UN in 1948; stated in the Council of Ministers that the Israeli Prime Minister should not forget that Israel had been “created by a decision of the UN”.

a5994.speaker: Benjamin Netanyahu, Israeli Prime Minister
a5994.speech: Replied that it was thanks to “the war of independence”; hit back, asserting that Israel was created by the war of independence of 1948, and not by a UN decision — a victory obtained “with the blood of heroic fighters, many of whom were Holocaust survivors”.

a5994.speaker: Denis Charbit, professor of political science at the Open University of Israel
a5994.speech: “Franco-Israeli relations are tense whenever Israel finds itself involved in a long-lasting conflict” ; “Western and European support is becoming more complicated. There will be no rupture of relations, but Macron could have said ‘Israel needs international legitimacy in order to exist’ — but that is not the same thing. Israel is not powerful enough in terms of area or population to stand alone against the whole world.”

a5994.speaker: United States
a5994.speech: On Tuesday, the United States warned Israel about the maintenance of American assistance in the absence of an improvement in humanitarian aid to Gaza.

a6054.speaker: “Dos Pobres para os Pobres” (book by Tânia Matsinhe)
a6054.speech: Says the informal sector in the country must be valued in order to fight poverty and accelerate economic development.

a6054.speaker: Roberto Albino, Minister of Agriculture, Fisheries and Environment of Mozambique
a6054.speech: Warns that the war in the Middle East could also affect the availability of fertilizers in the country; says that the ministry he heads is looking for solutions to prevent producers from being harmed by the difficulties in importing fertilizers.

a6054.speaker: Ministry of Health of Mozambique
a6054.speech: Intends, with the First Digital Health Conference in Mozambique (15–17 of this month), to seek tools to modernise services and ensure a reduction in demand and an increase in the services provided to users.

a6054.speaker: Daniel Chapo, President of the Republic of Mozambique
a6054.speech: During his audience with Cecília Sebastião Mathe (“Avó Cecília”), the Head of State praised her dedication, highlighted the positive impact of the initiative among children and encouraged her to continue with the mission.

a6054.speaker: Paul Kagame, President of Rwanda
a6054.speech: Appealed to Rwandans to reject groups that promote hatred between peoples; the remarks were made on Tuesday in Kigali, at the start of the hundred days of mourning in remembrance of one of the darkest pages in the country's history.

a6054.speaker: Women of the Tica Administrative Post, Nhamatanda district
a6054.speech: Ask for the establishment of vegetable-processing factories in that rural region to absorb their produce; the request was presented at the Mozambican Women's Day celebration organised by the local Government, where they also spoke of the need to strengthen the inclusion of women in different social spheres.

a6054.speaker: Daniel Chapo, President of the Republic of Mozambique
a6054.speech: Appeals to Mozambicans to prepare for a possible fuel crisis in the country; reaffirms that the country still has fuel reserves until the end of April but the stock may run out if the war in the Middle East persists.

a6424.speaker: Firmin Habumuremyi, permanent secretary of the communal administrator of Rugombo
a6424.speech: "Up to today, we have already recorded five deaths, four children and one adult. Which is so deplorable." He specified that according to medical tests these children died of measles, and stressed that the situation in which the refugees find themselves may also be a source of illness and death: "Truly, being a refugee is a misfortune. Indeed, when people flee en masse, they encounter many difficulties: fatigue, stress, trauma, etc. Many children arrived very tired, exhausted, starving, sick. It is really very sad."

a6424.speaker: Firmin Habumuremyi, permanent secretary of the communal administrator of Rugombo
a6424.speech: On hygiene: "It is really very difficult to have enough toilets for more than 20 thousand people. Yet it is normal that once people have eaten, they then need a place to relieve themselves." ; He acknowledges the hygiene situation has deteriorated since the arrival of the Congolese refugees: "We only have a few toilets at the schools. That cannot be enough. Which means that human faeces are found here and there. That causes the stench everywhere." ; Reported that on 19 February 2025 there was a meeting with UNHCR staff: "We received 25 mobile toilets given by Unicef. That has eased the ordeal a little, but it remains so insufficient. It is insignificant." ; Appeal: "If possible, the number of these mobile toilets must be increased, especially as the spaces where toilets should be dug are being used as shelter places for these refugees."

a6424.speaker: A refugee woman met at the Rugombo stadium (anonymous)
a6424.speech: "We live like animals. There is no more privacy. The worst is the lack of toilets. They installed mobile toilets, but they are insufficient and fill up very quickly. What is even more frustrating is that they are not emptied quickly. That makes the place unliveable." ; "In fact, during the day, we can move around and go and relieve ourselves in the surrounding dwellings or in the school toilets. But when that need arises during the night, it is agony. We have no other choice. We go right beside and do it."

a6424.speaker: Another Congolese refugee (anonymous)
a6424.speech: "It is serious. We are so numerous that respecting hygienic conditions is impossible. We run a great risk of diseases such as cholera."

a6424.speaker: A schoolgirl of Ecofo Rugombo II (anonymous)
a6424.speech: "We no longer study. Our schools are occupied. Yet other schools, other pupils are already preparing for the 9th-grade test. In any case, it will not be easy for us."

a6424.speaker: A pupil of the Rugombo II communal secondary school (anonymous)
a6424.speech: "Since the refugees sleep in our classrooms at night, there are no more classes in the morning. We wait for them to move their belongings and rearrange the classrooms. We come to study in the afternoon." ; "First, the place has become very smelly. Because they cook in front of the classrooms. There is no cleanliness any more. The toilets are overflowing, their children relieve themselves anywhere. It is really serious."

a6424.speaker: Felix Ndama, information officer at UNHCR and UNHCR focal point for the management of the Rugombo site
a6424.speech: "There are many risks. Because with bad weather, there is no joking. We try to advise, to guide. We keep on asking for help. Some families have blankets they brought from home, but they are few. But most have lost everything." ; Stressed that there is great concern about latrines: "Some organisations have brought mobile latrines which we try to place in the corners and also to maintain in order to avoid diseases such as cholera and others."

a6424.speaker: Egide Ndayishimiye, doctor of the Cibitoke health district
a6424.speech: Said those most exposed to disease are children, pregnant women and the elderly, and announced the establishment of mobile health centres in all the sites hosting refugees. "Owing to the lack of mosquito nets, malaria comes top of the diseases already recorded on site."

a6424.speaker: Brigitte Mukanga-Eno, UNHCR representative in Burundi
a6424.speech: Stated that 47,632 Congolese refugees have already been registered — 20,632 at the Rugombo stadium, 6,000 at the Rugombo II communal secondary school, 9,000 at Ecofo Rugombo II, 8,000 in various churches and 4,000 in the Cibitoke zone: "Among them there are 2,500 pregnant women, 7,000 children, 4 women who have suffered sexual violence and 3 cases of measles." On latrines, she explained only 35 mobile latrines are available, one for 50 people ; "Every day, new refugees arrive. It is a lot and the needs are enormous." Pregnant and breastfeeding women have specific needs, as do the 7,000 children registered: "Many are not with their parents. They came with neighbours. These are therefore children who need particular support."

a6424.speaker: Brigitte Mukanga-Eno, UNHCR representative in Burundi
a6424.speech: "Whether it be WFP, Unicef or UNHCR, we all need resources in order to be able to continue supporting this massive population in a decent and humane way. Compared with the refugee population Burundi had before, it really is the first time we have seen a crisis of this magnitude in more than 20 years." According to her, an immediate response is needed ; "We have put in place an inter-agency contingency plan so that, when the time comes, we can deploy it. The plan is there, but what we currently lack are the means to implement it." ; "Even to provide hot meals, the partners are overwhelmed. We call on all organisations to come and help support this response, if only to give meals to everyone, to provide these people with sanitary facilities in order to prevent further health catastrophes. It is really difficult. An immediate response is needed."

a6424.speaker: Brigitte Mukanga-Eno, UNHCR representative in Burundi
a6424.speech: On the refugees' routes and relocation: the refugees come essentially from two directions, the Rugombo axis made up of those who crossed the Ruzizi river on foot — "That is where we have the largest flow of people" — and the border at Gatumba: "There are also many Burundians who are returning. They were based in the DRC. Some are traders or farmers. But there is also a good portion of people who were refugees there and who are returning hastily because of the situation in the DRC. People are often eaten away by depression. There are people who suffered a great deal of violence or who saw members of their families executed before their eyes." ; Said the government has authorised the relocation of refugees to the Musenyi site in Rutana province and to Mwaro, and that relocation began last weekend with nearly 1,100 people moved to Musenyi: "The response is gradually being put in place but it is not yet sufficient. That is why we are asking all parties to accompany us in this process in order to carry out the transfer that has begun. Of course reception infrastructure is needed on the Musenyi side in Rutana, and also Mwaro, which is not yet developed at the moment, because it is an empty plot of land. It needs to be laid out and that requires a lot of resources." ; With the ministry, she said, "we are going to see how to set up catch-up schools quite quickly. But also, the most urgent thing for the moment is to finish the registration. As soon as we have data, we will transfer everyone to the Musenyi site in Rutana province and the Mwaro site, which are the two sites the government has allocated for the moment."

a6424.speaker: Congolese refugees (testimony, anonymous)
a6424.speech: Without specifying the number of victims, these refugees testify that during their crossing of the Rusizi river there were drownings.

a6424.speaker: Police sources in Rumonge
a6424.speech: According to police sources in Rumonge, arrests of returning Burundians whose identification is confusing are being carried out.

a6424.speaker: Leonard Niyonsaba, governor of Rumonge province
a6424.speech: Indicates that some of the consequences of the insecurity prevailing in neighbouring South Kivu are having repercussions on Rumonge province, and that a commission for the reception and management of problems resulting from the flow of refugees into Rumonge province has been set up; according to him, the province has a refugee transit centre on Mutambara hill where refugees are received before being transferred to the refugee camps in Rutana, Mwaro, Ruyigi and Muyinga provinces, and more than 200 Congolese refugees are gathered at the Rumonge stadium.

a6424.speaker: Civil society organisations (Rumonge)
a6424.speech: Indicate that the consequences of the insecurity in South Kivu province are very much felt in Rumonge, and stress that difficult conditions for receiving Congolese refugees are observed in Rumonge for those who have not had access to the UNHCR-managed refugee transit centre; the consequences will increase as long as the insecurity persists in South Kivu.

a6424.speaker: Brigadier General Gaspard Baratuza, spokesperson of the Burundi National Defence Force (FDNB)
a6424.speech: Speaking on RTNB on 24 February 2025, made it known that there is no crisis anywhere across the territory as far as security is concerned: "Security is good on the borders. Whether to the north, the south, the east or the west. The population goes about its daily business. There is no problem at all." ; He reassured Burundians that peace and security are a reality, while calling for vigilance: "If there is something wrong, it must be reported. That is what we ask of the population."

a6424.speaker: Brigadier General Gaspard Baratuza, spokesperson of the Burundi National Defence Force (FDNB)
a6424.speech: On President Ndayishimiye's speech denouncing Rwanda's intentions, stated that what the head of state raised is entirely logical and normal: "The Burundi national defence force goes about its business daily. In peacetime, soldiers prepare to wage war. And during war, they wage war. Today we are in a situation of complete calm, of peace. The soldiers are always at training. There are instruction centres, performance centres and specialised schools. That is all we do." ; "Should it happen that an enemy presents itself, our soldiers are always ready. You know, our soldiers are experienced. It is a professional army which has carried out quite a few internationally recognised missions." ; On the Somalia peacekeeping mission begun in 2007, "where our soldiers conquered very difficult zones by fighting and driving out al-Shabaab, which was feared by the international community. Today Somalia is calm thanks to the contribution of our soldiers. Being capable of restoring peace in a foreign country, one deduces that securing our own country is a simple consequence for the FDNB."

a6424.speaker: Brigadier General Gaspard Baratuza, spokesperson of the Burundi National Defence Force (FDNB)
a6424.speech: On messages circulating on social networks: "There are messages that intend to destabilise the population. We ask the population to remain calm at all times and to be always vigilant. Otherwise, everyone can see that these are erroneous messages. When it is said that the airport is under siege while planes are landing and taking off perfectly properly, you understand that the authors of these messages have other aims and are far from the truth. Let the population give no value to these messages!"

a6424.speaker: Evariste Ndayishimiye, President of Burundi
a6424.speech: In a speech in Kirundo province, denounced Rwanda's intentions to attack Burundi.

a6424.speaker: Police Lt. Col. Pierre Nkurikiye, spokesperson of the Ministry of the Interior, Community Development and Public Security
a6424.speech: Said the same the next day on RTNB: according to him, no one, whether from the AFC/M23 or from Rwanda, has attempted to attack Burundi. He asked Burundians to remain calm because, according to him, the security forces are perfectly prepared and capable of managing any situation.

a6494.speaker: Elijah Ngurare, Prime Minister of Namibia
a6494.speech: Stated that State and official funerals cost taxpayers N$38.4 million during the 2024/2025 financial year, that an additional N$2.5 million was spent on Heroes’ Day commemorations and that Independence Day celebrations cost the government N$25.6 million, revealing this while motivating the Office of the Prime Minister’s budget in the National Assembly: “In honouring our national heroes and celebrating our hard-won freedom, it was necessary to allocate resources to ensure these events are conducted with the dignity they deserve.”

a6494.speaker: Elijah Ngurare, Prime Minister of Namibia
a6494.speech: Revealed that of the total OPM budget, N$1.4 billion was dedicated to humanitarian assistance and resilience-building measures for communities affected by hardship, particularly drought; noted that N$1 billion was spent on food relief alone, N$86.7 million on the Commodity and Beneficiary Management Information System (CBMIS), N$86.7 million on livestock marketing support and N$87.9 million on water provision projects; added that the National Drought Programme will continue until 30 June 2025 with an additional N$200 million allocated: “Strengthening our national resilience to disasters and climate change is no longer optional. It is a necessity” ; “The OPM will also spearhead the finalisation of the National Drought Relief Programme, conduct the Annual Vulnerability Assessment and Analysis and establish the National Emergency Operation Centre.”

a6590.speaker: Divisional Commissioner Hamidou Diakité, head of the Sénou police station
a6590.speech: Said this dismantling illustrates once again the determination of the Defence and Security Forces to protect citizens and their property, in accordance with the directives of the country's highest authorities ; urged the population to be vigilant and to collaborate closely with the security forces in order to fight this type of crime effectively.

a6590.speaker: Police investigation (Sénou police station / Research Brigade findings)
a6590.speech: The investigations brought to light a particularly sophisticated modus operandi: the crooks targeted potential victims, won their trust, then impersonated third parties to induce them to make money transfers as part of fictitious transactions, mainly involving the supposed sale of rare and precious goods, notably Dogon masks presented as being of great value; once the victim was convinced, an accomplice posed as a "former supplier", followed by a third individual playing a "foreign buyer", with pretexts such as customs blockages or urgent fees used to justify new transfers. The investigation also revealed the international dimension of the network, which used SIM cards from Mali, Guinea-Conakry, the United Kingdom, the United States and France; among the victims is one N.C., defrauded of 47,225,000 CFA francs in a fictitious case involving three Dogon masks destined for a supposed European buyer.

a6645.speaker: Dr Adelheid Marschang, World Health Organization (WHO) senior emergencies officer
a6645.speech: According to her, the Democratic Republic of Congo is the country in the world with the highest number of people in need of humanitarian aid, some 25.4 million people ; at her meeting with the press corps accredited to the United Nations in Geneva she described the appalling humanitarian situation being witnessed in the DRC, explaining that "for decades, the conflicts in the mineral-rich east of the DRC have triggered alarming levels of violence, mass displacement, widespread disease, gender-based violence and severe mental trauma."

a6645.speaker: Dr Adelheid Marschang, World Health Organization (WHO) senior emergencies officer
a6645.speech: Said that more than 11,000 Mpox cases, including 443 deaths, have been reported this year, "mainly affecting children."

a6645.speaker: World Health Organization (WHO)
a6645.speech: Warned that the massive displacements place a severe strain on already fragile water and sanitation systems and add unsustainable pressure on limited local resources.

a6645.speaker: Scientists
a6645.speech: Last month sounded the alarm about a new dangerous strain of Mpox in South Kivu, fearing that it could spread in the overcrowded camps in and around the city of Goma.

a6645.speaker: Latest IPC (Integrated Food Security Phase Classification) report on chronic food insecurity
a6645.speech: According to the report, about 40% of the population, or 40.8 million people, suffer from severe food shortages, among whom 15.7 million face severe food insecurity, exposing them to an increased risk of malnutrition and infectious diseases; without immediate intervention more than one million children could suffer acute malnutrition.

a6645.speaker: Bruno Lemarquis, UN humanitarian coordinator in the Democratic Republic of Congo
a6645.speech: Last April had already noted with regret "over the last 10 years, a trend of underfunding of humanitarian action in the DRC."

a6645.speaker: Bintou Keita, Special Representative of the UN Secretary-General
a6645.speech: Told the United Nations Security Council that the activity of the M23 rebels presents a "very real risk of provoking a wider regional conflict."

a6645.speaker: UN group of experts
a6645.speech: According to the group, the militia is backed by Rwanda and is responsible for unlawful killings, rapes and other apparent war crimes in the DRC since late 2022.

a7231.speaker: Scholastica Nyenkan-Nimey, Deputy Minister for Administration at the Ministry of Commerce and Industry (Liberia)
a7231.speech: Praised the awardees for their commitment to paying taxes and emphasized the importance of compliance from businesses, institutions, and property owners across Liberia.

a7231.speaker: James Dorbor Jallah, Commissioner General of the Liberia Revenue Authority (LRA)
a7231.speech: Commended the taxpayers for their contributions to the national revenue, which supports Liberia's developmental programs; reiterated the LRA's commitment to reaching the $1 billion revenue mark, highlighting the role of technology in enhancing revenue collection and fiscal stability.

a7231.speaker: A representative of ArcelorMittal Liberia
a7231.speech: Expressed gratitude to the LRA for recognizing taxpayers and underscored the importance of tax compliance in driving national development; also commended the Liberian government for creating an enabling environment for businesses to thrive and pledged the company's continued commitment to meeting its tax obligations.

a7247.speaker: National Salaries, Incomes and Wages Commission (letter signed by Chairman Ekpo Nta)
a7247.speech: The approval for the increase of the corps members' allowance from N33,000 to N77,000 was contained in a letter dated September 25 2024, in line with the enactment of the National Minimum Wage (Amendment) Act 2024.

a7247.speaker: Federal Government of Nigeria
a7247.speech: Had, at that time, said the increase in the corps members' allowance was with effect from July 2024.

a7247.speaker: Brigadier-General Yushau Ahmed, Director-General of the National Youth Service Corps (NYSC)
a7247.speech: Announced on January 30 that corps members would begin to receive N77,000 as their monthly allowance from February 2025.

a7247.speaker: Corps members (collectively)
a7247.speech: Complained to Daily Trust that they still received N33,000 as allowance in February, and described the N33,000 allowance as insufficient for their basic needs, in lieu of the high cost of living in the country.

a7247.speaker: National Youth Service Corps (NYSC)
a7247.speech: When contacted, said modalities for the payment of the N77,000 allowance had been concluded, but said it was waiting for cash backing before paying the new allowance to corps members.

a7247.speaker: Caroline Embu, Acting Director, Information and Public Relations Department, NYSC
a7247.speech: "As soon as NYSC gets it (cash backing), we will start paying. We don't know when."

a7247.speaker: Bawa Mokwa, Director of Press, Office of the Accountant-General of the Federation
a7247.speech: When contacted on the telephone, promised to return with further details on the issue, but did not do so as of the time of filing this report.

a7247.speaker: Chinonso Udeh, corps member serving in Lapai, Niger State
a7247.speech: Said that he is currently struggling to cater for his daily needs as NYSC has continued to default in its promise to implement the new N77,000 allowance: "It hurts that NYSC has not paid us our new money. We have been dreaming of that money because it will help us a long way. All of us are just angry with the situation."

a7247.speaker: Chukuwuzulum Okechukwu, corps member serving in Kuje, Abuja
a7247.speech: "My prayer is that I should even enjoy the money before I pass out in June. They made us have long throat and now we can't see the money. They even assured us since that they will pay but everyday, excuses and it's not funny."

a7247.speaker: Olugbenga Adeyemi, corps member at Orozo, Abuja
a7247.speech: "We have lots of expenses and the economy is not funny. So we are seriously dreaming of the N77,000. Let them pay us and let's start enjoying it before we leave service."

a7247.speaker: Sunday Sado, corps member serving in Lagos
a7247.speech: "NYSC promised that February is the date they gave us that the payment will kick off so we are waiting for February allowance to see if it is the new amount that will reflect but disappointed."

a7247.speaker: Ibrahim Jimoh, corps member serving in Sokoto
a7247.speech: "The federal government has not started paying N77,000 and they are still paying N33,000."

a7247.speaker: Simi Aremu, corps member serving in Akwa Ibom
a7247.speech: "We were assured when we just entered camp this January that we will be earning our 77k soon. We don't know when soon is. Those who have been here since the announcement of N77,000 haven't received anything, we don't know what's happening."

a7247.speaker: Isah Gidado, corps member in Enugu State
a7247.speech: "We are the freshest corps members and we are hoping that they start paying the N77,000 soon so that I will enjoy the money for a long time. The economy is tough and we need more money to take care of ourself rather than depend on our family."

a7247.speaker: Mohammed Jamilu Mohammed, corps member serving in Osun State
a7247.speech: Decried: "I am really not happy about the way they are toying with us. Although they said February, so we're waiting and hoping. I have six months to go, so I want to enjoy the money very well before I go. Let them pay."

a7247.speaker: Peter Osaro, corps member serving in Katsina State
a7247.speech: "We would really appreciate the new increment, we are far from our family so we need enough for upkeep. We were so excited when we heard the news of the increment, but we haven't seen anything. I am not so disappointed because even the civil servants have not been paid the 70k salary."

a7247.speaker: Choyong Kenneth, corps member in Bayelsa
a7247.speech: "I was so excited to go for service because of the announcement of the N77,000 so I am hoping we will started receiving it from this February since the older corps members said they were expecting it from this month."

a7497.speaker: Donald Trump, US President (social media posts)

a7497.speaker: Dan Bongino, podcaster and newly appointed FBI deputy director (on his podcast)
a7497.speech: praised Patel and tried to allay Democratic fears the agency will be used to target Trump's enemies: "Kash Patel is there for one reason, he is there to make the FBI great again" ; He's committed to fighting crime and that only, he added, calling his new boss the "change agent" the FBI needs ; "How amazing would it be in four years to look back with a good, high-quality, reformed FBI free of woke culture and DEI that goes out making headline, big arrests of real bad guys destroying your community. How good would that be?"

a7497.speaker: Dan Bongino, podcaster and commentator (post on X)
a7497.speech: "EVERYONE involved in this DOJ/FBI abomination, from the management down to the agents, must be immediately terminated when the tyrants are thrown out of office."

a7497.speaker: Dan Bongino, conservative political commentator (2018)
a7497.speech: said, talking about his career as a prolific conservative political commentator: "My life is all about owning the libs now."

a7497.speaker: Kash Patel, FBI Director
a7497.speech: denied any plans to pursue political vendettas and has promised to "rebuild" the bureau.
